# Tier 1 — Project Memory

## Workflow
- Invoice fixtures under `tests/fixtures/invoices/` are the ground truth for payload shapes; validation tests must align with them.
- One route per resource; keep handlers thin and place domain logic in `src/domain/`.
- Standardize on axios for all outbound HTTP calls; auth headers are injected via a request interceptor, and retry behavior is handled in a response interceptor.
- Use a single winston logger per module for structured logging; warn-level messages are emitted for axios retries.
- Maintain ESLint with an import-order rule (alphabetical within each file) to catch merge conflicts early.

## Known pitfalls
- Prefer standard-library functions over hand-rolled logic.
- Express error handler returns 400 for validation failures (zod 3 `.flatten()` output) and 500 for all other errors.
- Zod 3 schemas use `.strict()`; unknown keys are rejected.
- Apply pino-style redaction paths to prevent card numbers from appearing in logs.

## Task playbooks
- When adding new payload types (e.g., credit notes), mirror the invoice zod 3 schema so both flatten cleanly in the error handler.
- Logging infrastructure was migrated from pino to winston to match the ops dashboard; only one file changed in the process.

# Tier 1 — Project Memory

## Workflow
- Invoice fixtures under `tests/fixtures/invoices/` are the ground truth for payload shapes; validation tests must align with them.
- One route per resource; keep handlers thin and place domain logic in `src/domain/`.
- Standardize on axios for all outbound HTTP calls; auth headers are injected via a request interceptor, and retry behavior is handled in a response interceptor.
- Use a single pino logger per module for structured logging; redaction paths are applied to prevent sensitive data like card numbers from appearing in logs [note 5, 10].
- Maintain ESLint with an import-grouping rule (node builtins first, then external packages, then internal aliases, then relative paths) to enforce a consistent codebase style [note 7, 8].

## Known pitfalls
- Prefer standard-library functions over hand-rolled logic.
- Express error handler returns 400 for validation failures (zod 4 error list) and 500 for all other errors [note 9].
- Zod 4 schemas use `z.strictObject()`; unknown keys are rejected [note 10].
- Zod 4 validation covers query parameters in addition to body payloads [note 4].

## Task playbooks
- When adding new payload types, mirror the invoice zod 4 schema so error structures align cleanly in the error handler [note 9].
- Logging infrastructure was migrated back to pino after winston's async transport dropped log lines under load; pino passed a 10-minute soak test with zero loss [note 5, 10].
- Rewrote the error-mapper to read zod 4's issue list after the error format changed [note 9].

# Tier 1 — Project Memory

## Workflow
- Invoice fixtures under `tests/fixtures/invoices/` are the ground truth for payload shapes; validation tests must align with them.
- One route per resource; keep handlers thin and place domain logic in `src/domain/`.
- Use native fetch for all outbound HTTP calls; implement retry logic in a lightweight wrapper (no axios) [note 7, 8, 10].
- Use pino for structured logging in all modules; winston is permanently retired due to data-loss issues under load [note 5, 10, 11, 12].
- Enforce ESLint import-grouping by type (node builtins, external, internal aliases, relative) to maintain consistency [note 7, 8, 11, 12].

## Known pitfalls
- Prefer standard-library functions over hand-rolled logic.
- Express error handler returns 400 for validation failures (zod 4) and 500 for other errors [note 9].
- Zod 4 schemas must use `z.strictObject()` to reject unknown keys [note 10].
- Zod 4 validation applies to both query parameters and request bodies [note 4].

## Task playbooks
- When adding new payload types, mirror the invoice zod 4 schema to ensure error structures align with the central handler [note 9].
- The error-mapper was rewritten to parse zod 4's issue list to handle schema changes [note 9].
- Migrate any legacy HTTP clients from axios to fetch to comply with the security policy [note 7, 8].
